reviews.text: I picked up this MacBook Neo last Tuesday at the Apple Store in downtown Chicago after months of waiting for the official launch. The starting price for the 1TB storage configuration is significantly higher than what I expected for a machine that doesn't even include a charging brick in the box. The build quality feels slightly cheaper than the Pro line with that aluminum chassis, but the premium pricing does at least guarantee a solid screen. My workflow integration with Docker and VS Code has been surprisingly seamless right out of the box on this new Apple Silicon chip. The thermal management is excellent and the battery easily lasts a full 12-hour coding session, which is definitely worth the investment. While the performance is top-tier, the lack of an SD card slot at this price point feels like a significant oversight for a pro machine. It is expensive to upgrade the RAM later, but the base unit handles compiling large React projects without any stuttering whatsoever. For the money, I wish the keyboard had more travel, but the trackpad responsiveness is undeniably the best I have ever used. I am definitely keeping this as my primary development rig despite the cost, especially since I finally ditched that clunky Linux setup I used for years.

At $1,499 for the 16-inch model with 32GB of unified memory, the MacBook Neo presents a competitive price point that matches its premium aluminum chassis and refined build quality.  Having traveled with a 1.8-kilogram Dell XPS 15 for the past three years, I was initially skeptical that Apple could reduce the weight to 1.14 kilograms without compromising structural integrity.  Furthermore, the 120Hz ProMotion display remains incredibly bright at 1000 nits during long layovers in terminal gates, while the M4 chip effortlessly handles multiple virtual machines and 4K video editing sessions without throttling.  Moreover, Apple's global support network has consistently delivered rapid repairs at their authorized service centers, ensuring that my workflow remains uninterrupted despite the high-volume travel schedule I maintain.
